text: Alethic (truth) pluralism, as developed by Crispin Wright and Michael Lynch, is best characterized as the view that:
choices: no statement in any domain is ever determinately true or false, since bivalence universally fails
a single substantive property, correspondence to fact, constitutes truth in every domain of discourse
'is true' is merely a device of disquotation and endorsement that ascribes no property whatever
truth is a single functional role that can be realized by different properties in different domains of discourse
explanation: Pluralism answers the 'scope problem' — correspondence fits physics but strains for ethics or mathematics — by holding that truth is one functional role (fixed by the platitudes) with domain-specific realizers, e.g. correspondence for the physical and superassertibility for the moral. Option 1 is the monist correspondence view pluralism rejects; option 2 is deflationism; option 0 wrongly conflates pluralism with a global denial of bivalence, which pluralism does not assert.
